audit_findings.title: Consolidated owner earnings may fund claims that do not belong to PMI common shareholders
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated cash-flow adjustments and reinvestment enter OE, while value per share uses only PMI common shares; any NCI-owned portion must be removed from OE or represented by an NCI bridge deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: United Arab Emirates-based Trans-Emirates Trading and Investments (FZC) ("TTI") holds a 33 % non-controlling interest in Philip Morris Misr LLC ("PMM"), an entity incorporated in Egypt which is consolidated in PMI’s financial statements in the SSEA, CIS & MEA segment.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated at the method level, although the required correction is unresolved. Filed 2025 earnings attributable to NCI were $500 million, equal to 5.0% of the $9,953.2 million anchor, and the audit reports a greater-than-5% earnings gap in seven historical years. Because the mismatch can affect both the anchor and trend, it is reasonably capable of materially changing modeled value.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct each OE year from net earnings attributable to PMI, allocate depreciation, capital expenditure and working-capital cash flows by ownership, then rerun the trend, anchor and all scenarios or deduct independently valued NCI claims in the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The deconsolidated RBH dividend may be embedded in the anchor while the RBH stake is also added
audit_findings.magnitude: $536 million of 2025 OE; conditional value impact of $6,376 million bear, $7,959 million base and $8,885 million bull, or $4.07, $5.08 and $5.68 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: A one-time RBH distribution may enter the 2025 OE anchor and be capitalized as recurring operating cash flow while the residual RBH investment is included in the stakes bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: On September 24, 2025, as permitted by the Plan, RBH paid a dividend of CAD $ 750 million (approximately $ 536 million) to PMI.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the $536 million dividend entered 2025 operating cash flow, but the supplied record does not establish whether the OE calculation purged it. If retained, it equals 5.4% of the anchor and reduces modeled operating value by about 5.4%, making this a material conditional error even though it would not reverse the present conclusion that price exceeds every scenario value.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $536 million through the 2025 OE worksheet, remove any retained amount, verify the June 2026 RBH value included within the $2,575 million stakes bridge, and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below price.

audit_findings.title: Russian cash may not be distributable excess cash worth par in the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $2.8 billion gross exposure; maximum $1.79 per share if written to zero
audit_findings.mechanism: Restricted or operating-required Russian cash may be overstated within the $5,999 million cash bridge addition.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, our Russian operations had approximately $4.8 billion in total assets, excluding intercompany balances, of which approximately $2.3 billion consisted of cash and cash equivalents held mostly in local currency (Russian rubles).
audit_findings.explanation: The June 2026 filing identifies $2.8 billion of Russian cash, 46.7% of bridge cash. Even a complete write-off would lower base value from $99.89 to approximately $98.10 per share, only 1.8%, and would leave it far below the $187.94 market price. The bridge classification still requires correction, but this exposure alone cannot change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the June 30, 2026 jurisdictional cash schedule, identify legally transferable and operationally excess balances, apply documented tax, currency and deprivation haircuts, and update the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Unaccrued tobacco and nicotine litigation is an omitted senior claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Unaccrued settlements, judgments and defense costs would reduce OE or the equity bridge, while commercialization restrictions could reduce growth and terminal cash flows.
audit_findings.evidence: Damages claimed in some of the tobacco-related litigation are significant and, in the case of the "Health Care Cost Recovery Litigation" described below, could range into the billions of U.S. dollars.
audit_findings.explanation: Pending litigation and the absence of most accruals are demonstrated, but no filed probability-weighted loss or reasonably estimable range exists. Claimed damages reaching billions do not establish expected loss, and the ZYN proceedings could also affect a major growth product. The record therefore supports a real valuation risk but cannot establish its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Prepare case-specific probability-weighted scenarios for the seven health-care recovery cases and pending ZYN matters, net them against existing accruals and insurance or indemnities, and rerun OE, growth and bridge values under those scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Underfunded employee-benefit claims may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.2 billion pension-plan deficit; $2.496 billion including filed postretirement and postemployment net liabilities, equal to a gross-test maximum of $1.59 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Any unfunded benefit obligation not already represented by future contributions in OE would require a bridge deduction; recurring contributions affect OE.
audit_findings.evidence: For pension plans with projected benefit obligations in excess of plan assets, the projected benefit obligation and fair value of plan assets were $8.8 billion and $7.6 billion, respectively, as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed underfunded-plan deficit is $1.2 billion. Adding the $260 million postretirement liability and $1,036 million postemployment liability produces a deliberately conservative $2.496 billion gross test, only 1.6% of base equity value and $1.59 per share. That scale cannot change the valuation conclusion, and a full deduction could double count liabilities already reflected through benefit expense and contributions.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the latest after-tax funded status and projected contributions to the OE calculation, determine which obligations are already captured in normalized cash costs, and deduct only the residual non-duplicative claim.

audit_findings.title: An equity-investee guarantee is not visibly netted against the stakes value
audit_findings.magnitude: $385 million maximum exposure, equal to $0.25 per share and 0.25% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: An expected loss on the Eastern investee guarantee would reduce the separately added stakes bridge value.
audit_findings.evidence: The maximum amount of these guarantee obligations is $385 million and they will be in effect until 2034.
audit_findings.explanation: Even assuming loss of the entire filed $385 million maximum guarantee, base value would decline only from $99.89 to approximately $99.64 per share and remain far below the $187.94 market price. The guarantee therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion on its own.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the June 2026 amount outstanding, guarantee terms, investee credit quality and whether the $2,575 million stakes value already incorporates the exposure; record any probability-weighted amount in the bridge.
